text:
Dmitri: heads up — ran into an edge case where soft-sharing a prefix between tenants caused a stale read after demote. steps to repro & thoughts below.
Liz: ugh. can you paste the minimal repro?
Dmitri: gist: tenant A holds prefix P in soft-share mode, tenant B requests ownership, demote sequence triggers but the in-flight reader on A still serves stale KV from its local slab.
Rahul: is this the case where demote only clears resident flag but doesn't drain pending readers?
Dmitri: exactly. demote clears residency bit and enqueues handoff, but readers that already checked residency then read from slab without re-checking epoch.
Sara: hmm. we thought the epoch/cas would protect that. sounds like a TOCTOU between residency check and read.
Dmitri: here's a simplified snippet of the problematic window:
```
// pseudo-code from runtime read path
if (is_resident(prefix)) {
  // reader continues reading from local slab
  value = slab.read(key)
  return value
}

// demote path
clear_residency(prefix)
enqueue_handoff(prefix)
```
Notice there's no fence after clear_residency to wait for inflight readers.
Liz: we could add a lightweight reader-writer fence or increment a generation counter on demote. readers snapshot generation at start and re-check after read.
Rahul: generation counters are cheap. pattern: readers read gen_before = gen.load(); read data; if (gen_before != gen.load()) retry or fallback.
Sara: retrying reads sounds ok for tail-latency sensitive paths? might bump p50/p95.
Dmitri: true — but we can piggyback: if generation mismatch, do a fast shadow read from stable store or route to fallback model variant. Only chance we pay cost is during ownership transitions which are rare.
Liz: alternative is to block demote until readers drain, but that stalls handoffs and hurts rebalancing.
Rahul: also multi-tenant sharing: if we force demote to wait, a noisy topology change could cascade. prefer reader-side retry.
Dmitri: another wrinkle: soft-share means we allow concurrent readers from old owner until hard eviction. If we add gen-counter, we must ensure it's updated only on hard-evict or when we make the slab invalid for reading.
Sara: proposal: maintain prefix.gen (u64). On demote -> prefix.gen++. Readers do: gen0 = prefix.gen; read slab; gen1 = prefix.gen; if gen0 != gen1 then fallback_read(). Fallback = route to authoritative node or read-through from backing store.
Liz: agree. also add a metric 'prefix.demote.gen_mismatch' to count how often we hit it.
Rahul: add a dogfooding canary: enable gen-check in a small ring with high-read, low-write tenants.
Dmitri: I'll throw together a spike and perf-run. quick k/v of config:
```
runtime.flags.prefix_gen_check=true
runtime.flags.prefix_gen_canary=[ring-3,ring-7]
```
Liz: don't forget to include stress tests: multiple concurrent readers + demote + burst handoffs.
Sara: ops-bot: create a canary playbook entry? @ops-bot please create ticket.
ops-bot: created #CANARY-912: "prefix-gen-check canary + playbook" assigned to @dmitri, due 2026-04-07 :white_check_mark:
Rahul: one more thought — telemetry: record latency delta when we fallback. if we see more than 1% of reads falling back we should consider alternate strategies.
Dmitri: noted. will log 'prefix.gen_mismatch' with tags {tenant, prefix_hotness, ring}.
Liz: sgtm. thanks — let's keep the demote fast; don't block handoffs. reader-side validation + fallback seems best tradeoff.
Sara: can you drop a short RFC blurb once the spike has numbers? i'll put it on the eng-runtime sync agenda.
Dmitri: will do, ETA EOD tomorrow with initial perf numbers.
Liz: :thumbsup:
